newsitem.title: USA: Tosco can't say how long Wilmington unit down.
newsitem.headline: Tosco can't say how long Wilmington unit down.

text.p: Tosco Corp said Friday that it was too early to tell how long a unit at its Wilmington, California plant, which was hit by fire on Thursday evening, would remain idled.

"Last night we did an assessment and didn't see any structural damage to the unit and had some determination that it was a pump in the unit that caused the fire," said Gary Gerstner, manager of human resources at the plant.
"There was no assessment about any more damage or about how long it would be down. The hydrocraker will remain down for an indeterminate time," he said.

The refinery, which was recently acquired from Unocal Corp., has an distillation capacity of nearly 120,000 and the hydrocracking unit, which upgrades distillates to lighter products, has a capacity of about 25,000 a day.
Gerstner said no other unit at the plant was affected by the fire.
There were no injuries in the fire, which was put out by 7.30 p.m. local time, and both Tosco and fire department monitoring detected no toxic emissions, Gerstner said.
The plant is located near Los Angeles and is connected by pipeline to Carson City.
